# s242 — init cannot choose the id prefix of a new queue

A new queue always gets the default scheme (prefix `S`, width 2), and no command can change it: `slicer init --id sp-01` fails with "'sp-01' is not an id of this scheme; expected the form S01", `id-prefix` only changes case, and `add --id sp-01` on a default queue mints a mixed-scheme id that fails `check`. The only route is hand-editing `id.prefix` in `.slicer/config.json` right after `init` (which S10 made effective), against the `slicer ai` rule never to edit tracking files.

**Findings:** squalor-xyz/suite field report (2026-10-09), squalplot queue · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

Per-product queues in one super-repo need distinct prefixes (`db-`, `st-`, `ob-`, `sp-`) so ids are unambiguous across queues and in commit messages. On 2026-10-09 the suite's new squalplot queue had to be seeded by hand: `slicer init`, then set `id.prefix` to `sp-` in `config.json` before filing anything. An agent following `slicer ai` cannot do that without an owner exception.

Suggested shape (to settle in the spec): an init option that takes the prefix and width (for example prefix sp- with width 2), and/or letting `init --id` set the scheme when the queue is empty. `id-prefix` could also accept a different prefix, not only a different case, while no item exists yet.

## Check

On an empty directory, the new init option (prefix sp-) gives `config id` = {"prefix":"sp-","width":2} and `next-id` = sp-01; `check` passes; a queue that already has items still refuses a prefix change.
